definition_en: Root class for records and concepts; not a table that must contain data.
Research study or cohort; distinct from a repository or paper.
Group within a study; retain the denominator and grouping criteria.
Participant identified within a study; do not automatically link people across studies.
A clinical event or record concerning a specific person.
A person's recorded condition or diagnosis; distinct from a shared disease concept.
A recorded symptom such as fever, cough, or shortness of breath.
An intervention or treatment described for a person; do not infer its timing.
A documented HCT/HSCT event; do not invent a date.
A CAR-T treatment event described in the source.
Drug treatment; preserve whether the source describes prescribing or administration.
Description of lung imaging findings; do not treat as a microbiology result.
An actual biological specimen; Sample is the corresponding former name.
A bronchoalveolar lavage specimen.
Blood specimen described in the methods; this alone does not establish a patient-level link.
Pleural fluid specimen mentioned in the methods; do not create individual specimens without evidence.
Swab specimen mentioned in the methods; preserve the reported type and collection site.
An individual test or assay, distinct from a shared method name.
An assay using sequencing.
Assay metagenomic next-generation sequencing.
Assay or processing that produces host gene expression; specimen and pipeline evidence is required.
Conventional microbiology test; a generic CMT record does not establish PCR or culture.
PCR described in the methods; assign to a person only with corresponding evidence.
Bacterial or fungal culture mentioned in the methods.
Microscopy or smear microscopy mentioned in the methods.
For example, galactomannan testing; do not equate with PCR.
Clinical laboratory testing; the source may describe it only at group level.
An SRA run; distinct from a patient, specimen, or assay.
Pipeline, software, and reference used to generate derived results.
A result or observation with a value, unit, measurement type, and status.
Detection of an organism or taxon; not proof that it causes disease.
Count associated with a gene and person or sample; not the number of gene copies in DNA.
Taxon abundance; retain unknown normalization formulas or units as unknown.
Coverage measurement; requires the metric definition and unit from the source.
Derived CNV feature or tumor fraction; distinct from gene expression.
CIBERSORTx cell-type score; do not automatically interpret as a percentage.
QC such as Q20, Q30, clean rate, or RMSE; attach to the correct run or pipeline.
Laboratory result such as WBC or ANC when individual values exist; group statistics belong in AggregateStatistic.
The entity or quantity measured; identify its namespace and classification level.
Gene concept; ENSG identifiers and gene symbols are not equivalent without verified mapping.
Organism or taxon concept; not automatically a pathogen.
Bacterial taxon with verified classification.
Viral taxon; examples in the sources include TTV and HHV6B.
Fungal taxon with verified classification.
Cell type estimated by a processing pipeline.
Chromosomal or CNV feature.
Laboratory analyte such as WBC, ANC, CRP, or PCT.
QC quantity such as Q20, GC, correlation, or RMSE.
Shared disease concept; a patient-specific occurrence belongs to an individual.
Shared treatment concept; distinct from an individual's treatment event.
Clinical assessment of a person or episode, with timing and adjudication method.
Diagnosis, infection status, and certainty as assessed in the source.
Source-adjudicated coinfection; do not infer it from the number of detected taxa.
Illness episode grouping multiple organisms; create only when episode boundaries are known.
Group-level value with a denominator; do not assign it to an individual.
Sensitivity, specificity, or agreement statistics; retain the reference standard.
Source file or version, with URI, checksum, license, and retrieval status.
Matrix with row and column meanings, feature namespace, and modality.
Exact location: sheet, row, column, XML ID or XPath, or verified PDF page.
A sourced statement with subject, predicate, and object or literal; traces individual attributes or edges.
External identifier with a namespace; BioSample, run, and PMCID use different namespaces.
Candidate link between two entities with verified, unresolved, or conflict status.
Paper or document with identifiers and versioned content.
Document section such as methods or results; preserve the source label.
Passage, table, figure, or cell used as evidence; does not automatically validate a claim.
Text passage with a location in a specific document version.
Table or cell region with headers and a defined scope.
Figure or caption; does not imply that image values have been extracted.
Statement attributed to an author or document, retaining context and certainty.
A paper's hypothesis; not a confirmed fact.
Statement about a study's methods.
Statement about a study's findings.
Citation record with citing paper, reference text, and target if resolved.
Many-to-many paper/concept mapping with relevance and provenance; distinct from citation.
Claim/evidence mapping with a supports, contradicts, or contextualizes role.
An award record keyed by award_key; not a Study or an individual annual funding record.
A funding/application record identified by appl_id and linked to an award; no assumption of additive budget scope.
An organization as reported within a source record; identical labels do not establish global identity.
An original person or organization name string in a stated role, without resolved identity.
A source-reported person name or incomplete name list; not a Patient and not a resolved unique person.
Source-reported city, state and country for an organization; not necessarily the study site.
A grant project-detail record or abstract; not a claim that full grant text is available.
A patent publication described by source metadata; scientific and legal claims are not inferred from metadata.
A reported patent classification code, preserving the source classification field.
A recorded search match connecting a document to a source-provided concept reference; not scientific support.
Unverified source taxon identifier(s) and label(s), preserving combined values without assuming namespace or alignment.
